def quick_new():
    """Quick-entry: seed a chat with the typed text (+ optional screenshot/url) and
    mark it as the session the main window should open. Targets an existing chat
    when `session` is a known id, otherwise spins up a fresh one."""
    global _pending_open

    sid = target if (target and target in _sessions) else _new_session()
    if text or screenshot or url:

    _pending_open = sid

1	# MIST Console
2	
3	A terminal-style desktop app for talking to Claude, built **from the ground up** so we own the entire UI. Instead of skinning the closed-source `claude` TUI, the Console runs the official `claude` binary **headlessly** and renders every pixel of the interface ourselves.
4	
5	## Why this architecture
6	
7	`claude`'s interactive TUI is a compiled binary we can't restyle. But the CLI exposes a full bidirectional streaming protocol:
8	
9	```
10	claude -p --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json --include-partial-messages --verbose
11	```
12	
13	So we run Claude as a long-lived subprocess that emits structured JSON events (init/capabilities, token-level text + thinking deltas, tool calls, tool results, usage, rate limits) and we render them however we want. The **brain stays Anthropic's** — we never reimplement it — so capability and correctness come for free, and we get total control of the surface.
14	
15	This hits the design criteria:
16	- **Fewest catastrophic errors** — leans on the official engine; one runtime; pure Python + web.
17	- **All the CLI capabilities** — tools, MCP servers, skills, slash commands, `/resume`, persona — all flow through the subprocess.
18	- **Easy to bolt features on** — Flask + plain web UI.
19	- **Low RAM** — one Python process + the system WebView (WKWebView). No Chromium, no Node. ~60–100MB vs Electron's 250MB+.
20	
21	## Architecture
22	
23	```
24	┌────────────────────┐     POST /send      ┌──────────┐   stdin (stream-json)   ┌────────────┐
25	│  WKWebView UI       │ ──────────────────▶ │  Flask   │ ─────────────────────▶ │  claude    │

The MIST **Console** is MIST's desktop chat surface: a from-scratch app that
renders Claude's full UI by running the official `claude` binary headlessly over
stream-json (Flask + WKWebView, all Python). It's the primary way Alex talks to
MIST face-to-face, alongside her cloned voice (`../mist-voice`).

The full app is NOT in this public harness. Like the voice **data**, it lives in
a separate **private** repo (it carries Alex's conversation-history layout,
greeting audio, and a fast-moving personal UI):

## → https://github.com/BaesTheorem/mist-console  (private)

Lives locally at: `~/Documents/mist-console`

## What's there
- `app.py` / `bridge.py` — Flask glue + the headless `claude` stream-json bridge
- `desktop.py` — native WKWebView window + the double-tap-⌥ quick-entry overlay
- `static/` — the UI (tab rail, pinned conversations, slash-command autocomplete, quickbox overlay + conversation picker)
- `mist-hotkey-agent.py` + `install-agent.sh` — always-on global-hotkey LaunchAgent
- `make-app.sh` — packages the clickable `.app` bundle
- gitignored even in the private repo: `data/` (conversation history), `greetings/`, `*.log`

## Seam with this harness
The Console reads MIST's persona system prompt at runtime from this harness:
`mist-terminal/mist-persona.md` (passed to `claude` via `--append-system-prompt-file`).
Keep that file in place or the Console falls back to a vanilla Claude voice.

## Rebuild
```bash
git clone https://github.com/BaesTheorem/mist-console.git ~/Documents/mist-console
cd ~/Documents/mist-console
uv run --script desktop.py     # run it, or ./make-app.sh to build the launcher
```
See the private repo's own `README.md` for the architecture + full setup.

Enter → `POST /quick-new {text, screenshot, url}` → `bridge.send(text, image_path, url)`: url appended as `[Current page: ...]`, screenshot read+base64 as an **image content block** (VERIFIED claude stream-json accepts image blocks — MIST described the diamond). 35

JS↔native via `WKUserContentController` message handler `mist` (`quickbox.html` posts `window.webkit.messageHandlers.mist.postMessage("surface"|"dismiss")`). `_show_panel`/`_hide_panel`/`_surface` (orderOut). `_quick_show` dispatches to main via `NSOperationQueue.mainQueue().addOperationWithBlock_` (the agent POSTs /show-quick on a worker thread; AppKit is main-thread only). `_surface` does NOT evaluate_js on main (deadlock) — relies on the main window's pollPending (1.5s) to jump to the new chat. GOTCHAS that killed the pywebview attempts: raw NSWindow mutations off the main thread throw "geometry should only be modified on the main thread" and SILENTLY fail; `.native` is None; off-screen-always-shown hits "Main window failed to start" before the shown event. **Quiet launch:** agent drops a `.quiet-launch` marker before `open`; `desktop.py` reads it (mtime <30s) → creates the main window `hidden=True`, so only the glowing overlay shows (main window reveals on Enter via `surface()`). Agent RETRIES `/show-quick` until 200 (show_quick registers in `_setup` a moment after Flask binds, so an immediate POST 503s). Overlay logo = official `mist-logo.png` (not the old ✦ glyph). Verified end-to-end via Quartz CGEvent synthetic double-tap: agent fires when MIST up AND relaunches MIST (~2s) when closed; launchd agent ax_trusted=True. Agent re-reads quick_access.json every 10s for the enable toggle.

40	**Quick Access (Spotlight-style glowing entry):** trigger = **double-tap the Option (⌥) key** (`quickaccess.py`: NSEvent global+local `flagsChanged` monitors, detect two Option-key-down transitions within 0.40s via keyCode 58/61 + Option flag 1<<19). Global monitoring REQUIRES macOS **Accessibility** permission — `ax_trusted()` + `request_permission()` (AXIsProcessTrustedWithOptions prompt) via ctypes into ApplicationServices/CoreFoundation (pyobjc ApplicationServices module absent, so ctypes). Settings panel shows enable toggle + a "Grant" button (POST `/quick-access/request-permission`) when untrusted; `/quick-access/diag` reports ax_trusted. The .app-launched process was NOT trusted by default → user must grant + relaunch. (History: started as NSEvent keyDown monitor (needed perm), then Carbon RegisterEventHotKey ⇧⌘M (perm-free, worked), now double-tap Option per Alex — back to needing Accessibility.) **CRITICAL deadlock fix:** the Carbon callback runs on the MAIN thread — calling pywebview `evaluate_js` there froze the UI run loop (window never painted). Fix: `_quick_show` only does `_activate()` + `_quick_window.show()` (no evaluate_js); the overlay focuses its own input via window `focus`/`visibilitychange`/`pageshow` listeners. (`QuickApi.surface()`'s evaluate_js is fine — js_api runs on a worker thread.) Transparency works (transparent=True frameless on_top); verified full flow via osascript: ⇧⌘M → glowing box → type+Enter → new chat titled with the text + main surfaces. Configurable in settings via `GET/POST /quick-access`, `data/quick_access.json`; `/quick-access/diag` for debug) → shows a SECOND pywebview window (`desktop.py` `_quick_window`: frameless+transparent+on_top, bottom-center, `static/quickbox.html`) — a rounded box with ✦ glyph + radiating MIST-blue glow (box-shadow + breathe animation). Type + Enter → `POST /quick-new {text}` (creates session, sends text, sets `_pending_open`) → `QuickApi.surface()` hides overlay, shows main window, calls `window.__syncPending`; main polls `GET /pending-open` (1.5s + on surface) to add+switch to the new chat. Esc → `QuickApi.dismiss()`. CAVEATS (untested live — Alex verifies): needs Input Monitoring permission (per-binary TCC, [[feedback_tcc_after_upgrade]]); hotkey doesn't consume the key, fires only when MIST backgrounded; quick-window bottom-center y-math (`_quick_position`, top-left coords) + pywebview macOS transparency may need tweaking; app must stay running (window-close still quits, no LSUIElement bg mode yet).
41	
42	**Auth = subscription, NOT API** (confirmed for Alex's "is this using API access?"): `apiKeySource: none`, no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, `overageDisabledReason: out_of_credits` = API overage disabled, runs on Claude subscription OAuth. Usage display is free, no API billing.
43	
44	**v1 caveat:** session runs `--dangerously-skip-permissions` (no permission UI yet, so tools don't hang). Phase 2 = interactive permission cards + mode switcher. Roadmap in README: permissions → slash palette → interrupt → diff viewer → image paste → MIST voice → resume.
45	
46	Distinct from [[project_mist_terminal]] (that's just a launcher wrapping Ghostty+real TUI; this owns the whole UI). Builds on [[reference_mist_branding]], [[project_mist_voice]].
